mainTopic: How an עבד עברי is acquired with money, and the argument over מוכר עצמו versus one sold by בית דין
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about the word הנעל in חליצה: the extra ה lets the word teach two lessons. Then a new משנה lists how an עבד עברי is acquired and goes free, adds the extra way an אמה עבריה goes free, and explains how a נרצע goes free. The גמרא looks for the source that a Hebrew slave is acquired with money. It moves step by step: from a slave sold to a נכרי, to the אמה עבריה (והפדה), to the male slave (a היקש), and finally to one who sells himself. That last case is learned either from the גזירה שוה of שכיר שכיר or from the 'ו' of וכי תשיג. The גמרא asks which תנא rejects שכיר שכיר and brings a ברייתא where the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר argue about four differences between מוכר עצמו and one sold by בית דין. רב טביומי in the name of אביי says that everyone accepts the גזירה שוה. On his view the differences come from specific פסוקים, like ועבדך שש שנים for the six-year limit and אזנו for piercing.

steps.title: The word 'the shoe' is needed to exclude heel-less sandals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges an earlier teaching from הנעל: that word is already needed to exclude sandals without heels.
steps.simpleTranslation: But that word is needed for sandals that have no heel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a challenge from the previous page. It says the word הנעל is already used up to teach that a heel-less sandal does not count for חליצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous page the גמרא learned a lesson from the word הנעל. Now it objects that this word already has another job: it excludes מסוליים, sandals with no heel. If the word is busy with that job, maybe it cannot also teach the earlier lesson.

keyTerms.meaning: Sandals or slippers with no heel, which do not count as a proper shoe
'The shoe', the word from the פסוק of חליצה (דברים 25:10)

phrases.english: [It is needed] for sandals that have no heel!
phrases.notes: The start of this question is on the previous page. The גמרא means the word הנעל is needed to exclude these sandals from חליצה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the challenge begun on the previous page about the word הנעל.
steps.kashyaTarget: The earlier lesson learned from the word הנעל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: One word cannot teach two things. Since הנעל is needed to exclude heel-less sandals, it is not free to teach the earlier lesson.

steps.title: The extra ה teaches both lessons
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק could have written נעל, so the extra ה in הנעל allows two lessons.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the פסוק should write 'shoe'. Why does it say 'the shoe'? Learn two things from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The plain word נעל would be enough to exclude heel-less sandals, so the extra ה gives us room for the second lesson.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Just to exclude sandals with no heel, the תורה only needed the word נעל, since such a sandal is not a real shoe. The added ה makes it הנעל, and this extra letter is the source for another lesson. So both lessons come from this word, and the challenge falls away.
steps.whatToRemember: An extra letter in a פסוק can be the source for an additional lesson, so one word can teach two things.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write 'shoe';
what is [the point of] 'the shoe'?
Learn two [things] from it.
phrases.notes: The two lessons are the one from the previous page and this one about heel-less sandals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 1.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Extra wording: the extra ה shows that the word teaches more than one thing
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word הנעל is fully used up excluding heel-less sandals.
steps.terutzMaskana: The plain word נעל would exclude the sandals. The extra ה allows a second lesson, so both lessons stand.

steps.title: משנה: How a Hebrew slave and maidservant are acquired and go free
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists two ways an עבד עברי is acquired and three ways he goes free. An אמה עבריה has one more way to go free: סימנין.
steps.simpleTranslation: A Hebrew slave is acquired with money or with a document. He gains his freedom with years, with יובל, or by paying off what is left of his value. A Hebrew maidservant has one more way than he does: she goes free when she shows signs of maturity.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It lists how a Hebrew slave becomes a slave and the ways he goes free, and adds an extra way out for a Hebrew maidservant.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two ways in: כסף (money) and שטר (a document). There are three ways out: finishing six years, the arrival of יובל, or גרעון כסף, which means paying back the value of the years that remain. An אמה עבריה also goes free when she shows סימנין, the signs of physical maturity.

keyTerms.meaning: The fiftieth (Jubilee) year, when slaves go free
Deducting money: paying back the value of the years that remain

steps.confusionAlert: 'קונה עצמו' does not mean he buys himself as a slave. Here it means he gains himself back, so he goes free.

phrases.english: MISHNA: A Hebrew slave is acquired
through money and through a document,
and he acquires himself through years,
phrases.notes: 'Years' means finishing his six years of work.

phrases.english: and through the Jubilee, and through deduction of money.
A Hebrew maidservant has more than him,
for she acquires herself through signs [of maturity].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה. The topic moves from יבמה to עבד עברי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An עבד עברי is acquired with כסף or שטר and goes free with six years, יובל, or גרעון כסף. An אמה עבריה can also go free with סימנין.

steps.title: משנה: The pierced slave
steps.stepSummary: A נרצע is acquired through רציעה and goes free only at יובל or when the master dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: A pierced slave is acquired by having his ear pierced. He goes free at יובל or when the master dies.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the נרצע, a slave who chose to stay after six years and had his ear pierced. It tells us how he goes free.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The piercing (רציעה) is what keeps the slave bound beyond his six years. After that, years no longer free him. He goes out only at יובל or at the death of the master.

keyTerms.meaning: A slave whose ear was pierced so that he stays on after six years
Piercing the ear with an awl

phrases.english: The pierced one is acquired through piercing,

phrases.aramaic: וְקוֹנֶה אֶת עַצְמוֹ בַּיּוֹבֵל, וּבְמִיתַת הָאָדוֹן.
phrases.english: and he acquires himself through the Jubilee and through the death of the master.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה with a related type of slave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A נרצע is acquired through רציעה and goes free at יובל or at מיתת האדון.

steps.title: Where do we learn that a Hebrew slave is acquired with money?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks for the source that an עבד עברי is acquired with כסף.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: A Hebrew slave is acquired with money. From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts working on the משנה. It quotes the first rule and asks which פסוק teaches it, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה stated that money acquires a Hebrew slave but gave no source. The גמרא wants to find where this comes from in the תורה.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
From where do we know this?

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ עֶבֶד עִבְרִי נִקְנֶה בְּכֶסֶף. מְנָלַן?
phrases.english: GEMARA: A Hebrew slave is acquired through money. From where do we [know this]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first rule in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק that teaches that an עבד עברי is acquired with money.

steps.title: The source is 'from the money of his purchase'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings the פסוק מכסף מקנתו as proof that a Hebrew slave is acquired with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'from the money he was bought for', which teaches that he is acquired with money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק. It speaks of the money paid to buy the slave, so we see that he is bought with money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words מכסף מקנתו describe the money of his purchase. This shows that money is a way to acquire him. The next step will ask whether this פסוק covers every case.

keyTerms.meaning: From the money of his purchase

phrases.english: The verse states: 'From the money of his purchase'
teaches that he is acquired through money.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק מכסף מקנתו shows that an עבד עברי is acquired with money.

steps.title: That פסוק only covers a slave sold to a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that the פסוק is about a slave sold to a נכרי, who acquires everything with money. What is the source for a slave sold to a Jew?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found this for a Hebrew slave sold to a non-Jew, since a non-Jew acquires everything with money. From where do we know it for a slave sold to a Jew?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. The פסוק it brought speaks about a slave sold to a non-Jew, so it may not apply to a Jewish buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A non-Jew acquires all things with money, so it is no surprise that he buys a slave with money too. A Jew might be different, since he might need some other kind of קנין. So the גמרא still needs a source for a Hebrew slave sold to a Jew.

phrases.english: We have found a Hebrew slave
who is sold to a non-Jew,
since all his acquisition is through money;
[one] sold to a Jew, from where do we [know]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the proof from step 6 to a non-Jewish buyer.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק is about a נכרי, and money is the only way a נכרי acquires anything. That does not prove a Jew can acquire a slave with money.

steps.title: Proof from 'and he shall let her be redeemed'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings והפדה about the אמה עבריה: she deducts from her redemption price and goes free, which shows she was bought with money.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says 'he shall let her be redeemed'. This teaches that she subtracts from her redemption price and goes free.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק about a Hebrew maidservant sold to a Jew. She can free herself by paying the value of the time she has left.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her early release works by money: her purchase price, minus the time she has already served. That shows money was the way she was acquired in the first place, and here the buyer is a Jew. So the source for a Jewish buyer acquiring with money comes from the אמה עבריה.

keyTerms.meaning: And he shall let her be redeemed

steps.whyThisMatters: This gives the source for the משנה's rule that an עבד עברי is acquired בכסף even when the buyer is a Jew. It also explains the משנה's way out called גרעון כסף.

phrases.english: The verse states: 'And he shall let her be redeemed'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:8, about an אמה עבריה sold to a Jew.

phrases.english: teaches that she deducts from her redemption [price] and goes out [free].

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 7 by bringing a פסוק about a Jewish buyer.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: והפדה shows that an אמה עבריה sold to a Jew goes free by paying her price minus the time she served. So she was acquired with money.

steps.title: The maidservant proof may not cover a male slave
steps.stepSummary: The proof from אמה עבריה might only work for a woman, since a woman can be married with money. So where do we learn that a male עבד עברי is acquired with money?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found this for a Hebrew maidservant: since she can be betrothed with money, she can be acquired with money. But a Hebrew slave, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from step 8. It argues that the maidservant might be a special case, so the male slave still needs his own source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman can be acquired for קידושין with money, so it makes sense that she can also be bought as a maidservant with money. A man has no such parallel. So the proof from the אמה עבריה does not automatically carry over to the עבד עברי.

keyTerms.meaning: We found (a source for one case)

phrases.english: We found this for a Hebrew maidservant,
phrases.notes: He means the proof from 'והפדה' in the last step.

phrases.english: since she can be betrothed with money,
she can be acquired with money.
But a Hebrew slave, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אשכחן אמה העבריה הואיל ומיקדשה בכסף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the proof of step 8 to women only
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from אמה עבריה in step 8
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A woman's acquisition with money may come from her ability to be married with money, which a man does not have.

steps.title: The verse compares the Hebrew man to the Hebrew woman
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts העברי and העבריה side by side, so whatever works for her works for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'If your brother, the Hebrew man or the Hebrew woman, is sold to you, and he shall serve you six years.' It compares the Hebrew man to the Hebrew woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the תורה itself puts the male and female slave in one phrase. That links their laws together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a היקש, a comparison made because the פסוק lists them together. Since the woman is acquired with money, the man is too. Her special reason no longer matters, because the תורה tied them together.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares, by putting things side by side in a פסוק (a היקש)

phrases.english: The verse says:
"If your brother, the Hebrew man, is sold to you
or the Hebrew woman
and he shall serve you six years"
It compares the Hebrew man to the Hebrew woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר קרא כי ימכר לך אחיך העברי או העבריה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A היקש: the פסוק lists the Hebrew man together with the Hebrew woman, so he too is acquired with money.

steps.title: A slave sold by the court may not cover one who sells himself
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק in דברים is about a slave sold by בית דין, who is sold against his will. Maybe that is why money works for him. Where do we learn it for מוכר עצמו?
steps.simpleTranslation: We found this for one whom the court sold: since he is sold against his will, money works. But one who sells himself, where do we learn it from?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises another limit on the proof. The verse it just used talks about a slave sold by בית דין, and that might be different from a person who sells himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A slave sold by בית דין is sold against his will, so perhaps the תורה lets money acquire him more easily. A person who sells himself chooses to do it, which is a different situation. So he still needs his own source.

keyTerms.meaning: The court sold him (a thief who cannot pay back what he stole)

phrases.english: We found this for one whom the court sold,
phrases.notes: The verse in דברים is about a thief whom בית דין sells to repay what he stole.

phrases.english: since he is sold against his will.
But one who sells himself, from where do we know it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אשכחן מכרוהו בית דין הואיל ונמכר בעל כורחו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the proof of step 10 to one sold by בית דין
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from דברים 15:12 in step 10
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone sold against his will may be a special case. That does not prove anything about a person who sells himself willingly.

steps.title: A גזירה שוה from the word 'hired worker'
steps.stepSummary: The word שכיר appears both for one sold by בית דין and for מוכר עצמו. This links the two cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: He learns it from 'hired worker' and 'hired worker.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a גזירה שוה. The same word, שכיר, appears in both sections, so they share the same law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In ויקרא, one who sells himself is called a שכיר. In דברים, one sold by בית דין is also described with the word שכיר. This shared word carries the rule of acquiring with money over to מוכר עצמו.

keyTerms.meaning: A link between two places in the Torah that use the same word

phrases.english: He learns it from "hired worker" and "hired worker."
phrases.notes: The word shows up in both places: ויקרא 25:40 (selling himself) and דברים 15:18 (sold by the court).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A גזירה שוה of the word שכיר links one who sells himself to one sold by בית דין.

steps.title: What about the opinion that rejects this גזירה שוה?
steps.stepSummary: The answer of step 12 only works for someone who accepts the גזירה שוה of שכיר שכיר. What is the source for the one who does not?
steps.simpleTranslation: This works well for the one who learns 'hired worker' from 'hired worker.' But for the one who does not learn it, what is there to say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that not everyone accepts the שכיר שכיר link. So it asks what source the other opinion would use, and this sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is an opinion that does not learn this גזירה שוה. For him, step 12's answer falls away. He still needs a different source for מוכר עצמו being acquired with money.

keyTerms.meaning: This works out well (for one view)
For the one who does not derive

phrases.english: This works well for the one who learns "hired worker" from "hired worker,"
but for the one who does not learn "hired worker" from "hired worker,"
what is there to say?

steps.triggerLanguage: הניחא למאן דיליף שכיר שכיר אלא למאן דלא יליף שכיר שכיר מאי איכא למימר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that step 12's answer only works for one opinion
steps.kashyaTarget: The גזירה שוה answer of step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: An opinion that rejects the שכיר שכיר link has no source yet for מוכר עצמו.

steps.title: The 'and' in 'וכי תשיג' links the two sections
steps.stepSummary: The section about a slave sold to a נכרי begins with 'וכי', meaning 'and if'. That 'and' joins it to the section before it about מוכר עצמו to a Jew, so the earlier section learns from the later one.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says 'And if [a stranger] becomes rich.' The 'and' adds onto the first topic, so let the upper section be learned from the lower one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new source for the opinion that rejects the גזירה שוה. It uses the extra letter 'ו' to connect two neighboring sections of the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The section about a Jew sold to a נכרי (ויקרא 25:47) starts with 'and'. That ties it to the section just above it, about a Jew who sells himself to a Jew. As step 7 said, a נכרי acquires with money. So the one who sells himself to a Jew is also acquired with money.

keyTerms.meaning: The 'and' adds onto the earlier topic
The upper (earlier) section learns from the lower (later) one

steps.whatToRemember: Every type of עבד עברי is acquired with money. The אמה עבריה is learned from 'והפדה'. The man is learned from the היקש to her. One who sells himself is learned either from the גזירה שוה of שכיר שכיר or from the 'ו' of 'וכי תשיג'.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Upper' and 'lower' mean the order of sections in the פסוקים, not importance. The upper section (selling himself to a Jew) learns from the lower one (sold to a נכרי).

phrases.english: The verse says: "And if [a stranger] becomes rich"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 25:47. This opens the section about a Jew sold to a נכרי.

phrases.english: the 'and' adds onto the first topic,
phrases.notes: The first topic is the section right before it, about a Jew who sells himself to a Jew.

phrases.english: so let the upper section be learned from the lower one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר קרא וכי תשיג מוסף על ענין ראשון
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 13
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The 'ו' of 'וכי תשיג' joins the section about a slave sold to a נכרי, who is acquired with money, to the section about one who sells himself to a Jew. So he too is acquired with money.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Even without the גזירה שוה, one who sells himself is acquired with money, learned from the slave sold to a נכרי.

steps.title: Which תנא Does Not Learn the Hired Worker Link?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who the תנא is that does not learn the גזירה שוה of שכיר שכיר.
steps.simpleTranslation: And who is the תנא who does not learn the link between 'hired worker' and 'hired worker'?
steps.whatsHappening: Step 13 mentioned a person who does not accept the שכיר שכיר link. Now the גמרא asks who that person actually is, and it will answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now that opinion was only a possibility. The גמרא wants to show that a real תנא holds it, so the discussion is not just theory.

keyTerms.meaning: A sage from the time of the משנה
Hired worker; the word that links the two kinds of slave
Linking two cases through the same word in the תורה

phrases.english: And who is the tanna
who does not learn "hired worker" "hired worker"?
phrases.notes: This is the word link from step 12 that joins מוכר עצמו to one sold by בית דין.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the opinion mentioned in step 13 and asks who holds it.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The identity of the תנא who rejects the גזירה שוה of שכיר שכיר.

steps.title: A ברייתא: Self-Sold Slave Can Be Sold for More Than Six Years
steps.stepSummary: It is the תנא of a ברייתא who says that מוכר עצמו can be sold for more than six years, but one sold by בית דין only for six.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: One who sells himself is sold for six years or more than six. If בית דין sold him, he is sold only for six.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers by quoting a ברייתא. Its first rule is that a man who sells himself may agree to serve longer than six years, while one sold by בית דין serves only six.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This תנא treats the two kinds of slave differently. That suggests he does not link them through the word שכיר. More differences follow in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: One who sells himself as a slave
בית דין sold him, to repay what he stole

phrases.english: It is this tanna,
as it is taught in a baraita:
One who sells himself is sold for six years,
and for more than six,
if the court sold him,
he is sold only for six.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 15 by quoting a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The תנא קמא of this ברייתא, who separates the laws of the two kinds of slave.

steps.title: Three More Differences Between the Two Slaves
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: only one sold by בית דין has his ear pierced, receives a parting gift, and may be given a Canaanite maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: One who sells himself is not pierced; one sold by בית דין is pierced. One who sells himself gets no parting gift; one sold by בית דין gets a gift. One who sells himself is not given a Canaanite maidservant by his master; one sold by בית דין is given one.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא lists three more laws that apply only to the slave sold by בית דין and not to the man who sold himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Together with the six years, that makes four differences. The תנא קמא clearly keeps the two kinds of slave apart in every area.

keyTerms.meaning: Has his ear pierced with an awl
They give him a parting gift when he goes free

phrases.english: One who sells himself is not pierced,
phrases.notes: This is the slave who wants to stay past his time and has his ear pierced at the door.

phrases.english: if the court sold him, he is pierced.
One who sells himself is not given a parting gift,
if the court sold him, he is given a parting gift.

phrases.aramaic: הַמּוֹכֵר עַצְמוֹ אֵין רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ
phrases.english: One who sells himself, his master does not give him
a Canaanite maidservant,
if the court sold him,
his master gives him a Canaanite maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues quoting the ברייתא begun in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the תנא קמא, piercing, the parting gift, and the Canaanite maidservant apply only to one sold by בית דין.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר: Both Slaves Are the Same
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר holds that both kinds of slave are equal in all four laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר says: Both are sold only for six years, both are pierced, both get a parting gift, and both may be given a Canaanite maidservant by their master.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now brings רבי אלעזר, who disagrees with all four differences and treats both slaves the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי אלעזר, whatever applies to one sold by בית דין applies to מוכר עצמו too. This sets up the גמרא's guess in the next step about why they argue.

keyTerms.meaning: This one and that one, meaning both

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar says:

phrases.aramaic: זֶה וָזֶה אֵינוֹ נִמְכָּר אֶלָּא לְשֵׁשׁ,
phrases.english: Both this one and that one are sold only for six years,
both this one and that one are pierced,
and both this one and that one are given a parting gift,

phrases.aramaic: וְזֶה וָזֶה רַבּוֹ מוֹסֵר לוֹ שִׁפְחָה כְּנַעֲנִית.
phrases.english: and for both this one and that one, his master gives him a Canaanite maidservant.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view in the same ברייתא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מוכר עצמו and one sold by בית דין are equal in all four laws.

steps.title: Is Their Argument About the Hired Worker Link?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests that the תנא קמא rejects the גזירה שוה of שכיר שכיר and רבי אלעזר accepts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it not about this that they argue: the תנא קמא does not learn 'hired worker' from 'hired worker', and רבי אלעזר does?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests a reason for the argument. The תנא קמא would be the one who does not use the שכיר link, which would answer step 15.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If you use the word link, the two slaves are joined and share all their laws, which is רבי אלעזר's view. If you do not, they stay separate, which is the תנא קמא's view. This is only a suggestion, and the next step will challenge it.

keyTerms.meaning: Is it not so that...? A suggested reading

phrases.english: What, is it not about this that they argue,
that the first tanna does not learn "hired worker" "hired worker",
and Rabbi Elazar learns "hired worker" "hired worker"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from the argument in the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: That a real תנא (the תנא קמא) rejects the גזירה שוה of שכיר שכיר.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The argument between the תנא קמא and רבי אלעזר in the ברייתא.

steps.title: רב טביומי: Everyone Learns the Link; They Argue About a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב טביומי in the name of אביי says that both תנאים accept the גזירה שוה, and their argument is about how to read a certain פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב טביומי said in the name of אביי: Everyone learns 'hired worker' from 'hired worker'. Here they argue about this פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the suggestion of step 19. It says the תנא קמא also accepts the שכיר link, and the argument comes from somewhere else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides start with the two slaves linked. The תנא קמא, however, finds a פסוק that limits certain laws to one sold by בית דין. That means the ברייתא does not prove that anyone rejects the גזירה שוה.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the תנא קמא rejects the שכיר link. According to רב טביומי he accepts it, but a separate פסוק limits it in these specific laws.

phrases.english: Rav Tavyumei said in the name of Abaye:
Everyone learns "hired worker" "hired worker",
and here they argue about this verse:

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב טָבְיוֹמֵי מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּאַבָּיֵי: דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא יָלֵיף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggested reading of the argument in step 19.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the idea that the ברייתא's argument is about the גזירה שוה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The argument can be explained by how each תנא reads a פסוק, even though both accept the שכיר link.

steps.title: The תנא קמא's Source: 'He Shall Serve You Six Years'
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא reads 'ועבדך שש שנים' as limiting the six-year cap to one sold by בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the תנא קמא, who says that one who sells himself can be sold for six years or more? The תורה limited it in the case of one sold by בית דין: 'and he shall serve you six years.' This one, and not one who sells himself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב טביומי begins explaining the four differences one by one. First he explains the six-year rule from a פסוק about the slave sold by בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק 'ועבדך שש שנים' is said about one sold by בית דין, and the תנא קמא reads it as 'only this one'. So even with the שכיר link, the six-year cap does not apply to מוכר עצמו, and he may agree to serve longer.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה limited it, leaving a case out
And he shall serve you six years

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows how a גזירה שוה can be accepted in general yet still have limits when a פסוק specifically leaves a case out.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first tanna
who says that one who sells himself
is sold for six years and more than six?

phrases.aramaic: מִיעֵט רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי מְכָרוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין:
phrases.english: The Merciful One limited it regarding one sold by the court:
"And he shall serve you six years"
this one, and not one who sells himself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts to back up step 20 by showing the פסוק behind the תנא קמא's first difference.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The six-year limit is restricted by 'ועבדך שש שנים' to one sold by בית דין, so מוכר עצמו may serve longer.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר uses 'and he shall serve you' for a different lesson
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר reads ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ as teaching that a slave serves 'you', the master, and not an heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי אלעזר, says: 'And he shall serve you' means he serves you and not your heir.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what רבי אלעזר does with the word ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״, since he does not use it to limit the six years to one sold by בית דין.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 21 showed that the תנא קמא learns from ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ that only one sold by בית דין has the six-year limit. רבי אלעזר does not need the word for that. He uses it to teach that a עבד עברי does not pass to an heir. So both sides use the word, just for different lessons.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the other opinion)

phrases.english: And the other one:
phrases.notes: This means רבי אלעזר, the one who did not use the word for the six-year rule.

phrases.english: 'And he shall serve you' —
you, and not an heir.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי אלעזר's use of the same word that the תנא קמא used in step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר uses ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ to teach that a slave is not passed to an heir.

steps.title: Where does the תנא קמא learn the heir rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where the תנא קמא learns that a slave is not passed to an heir.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, the תנא קמא, where does he learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to the תנא קמא: he used ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ for the six-year rule, so where does he learn the heir rule? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Presumably the תנא קמא also agrees that a slave does not pass to an heir. But he already used the word for something else. So the גמרא asks for his source.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Now 'the other one' is the תנא קמא. Where does he learn 'and not to an heir'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks the תנא קמא for the source of the lesson רבי אלעזר just took from the word.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The תנא קמא's source for the rule that a slave does not pass to an heir.

steps.title: The word 'and he shall serve you' appears a second time
steps.stepSummary: The תנא קמא learns the heir rule from a second time ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ is written.
steps.simpleTranslation: Another 'and he shall serve you' is written in the תורה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the word ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ shows up in another פסוק too, and the תנא קמא learns the heir rule from there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two places with this word. The תנא קמא uses one for the six-year rule and the other for the heir rule. So he loses nothing.

phrases.english: Another 'and he shall serve you' is written.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A second appearance of ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ teaches the תנא קמא the heir rule.

steps.title: What does רבי אלעזר do with the second word?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי אלעזר does with the second ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other one, רבי אלעזר, what does he learn from that second verse?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא goes back to רבי אלעזר. If there is a second ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״, why doesn't he use it for the six-year rule? This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the second word were free, רבי אלעזר could have learned the תנא קמא's lesson from it too. The גמרא needs to show that he uses it for something else.

phrases.english: And the other one?
phrases.notes: Back to רבי אלעזר. What does he do with the second ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how רבי אלעזר uses the second word mentioned in step 24.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What רבי אלעזר learns from the second ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״.

steps.title: The second word comes to make the master feel at ease
steps.stepSummary: For רבי אלעזר, the second ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ is there to calm the master about setting the slave free.
steps.simpleTranslation: That verse comes to make the master feel at ease.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר uses the second word for a different purpose: to make the master feel good about letting the slave go.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since רבי אלעזר uses the second word for הרצאת אדון, it is not free to teach the six-year rule. Each side has now been shown to use both appearances of ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״. This finishes the explanation of the six-year difference; the next step moves on to piercing.

keyTerms.meaning: Making the master feel at ease

steps.whatToRemember: According to רב טביומי, both תנאים accept the גזירה שוה. On the six-year rule, they argue over which lesson each ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ teaches: the six-year limit, no passing to an heir, or calming the master.

phrases.english: That one
comes to make the master feel at ease.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 and closes the explanation of how each תנא reads the פסוקים.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר uses the second ״וַעֲבָדְךָ״ for הרצאת אדון.

steps.title: Why is one who sells himself not pierced?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason the תנא קמא says a מוכר עצמו is not pierced.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason of the תנא קמא, who says one who sells himself is not pierced?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new question about another of the laws in the ברייתא: piercing the ear. This sets up the source that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 17 the תנא קמא said that only one sold by בית דין is pierced. Now the גמרא wants to know which פסוק leaves out a מוכר עצמו.

phrases.english: What is the reason of the first תנא
who says one who sells himself is not pierced?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא דְּתַנָּא קַמָּא דְּאָמַר מוֹכֵר עַצְמוֹ אֵינוֹ נִרְצָע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the six-year rule to the rule of רציעה in the same ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that a מוכר עצמו is not pierced.

steps.title: 'His ear' leaves out one who sells himself
steps.stepSummary: The word ״אָזְנוֹ״ in the piercing פסוק means the ear of one sold by בית דין, not the ear of a מוכר עצמו.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because the תורה limited it in the case of one sold by בית דין: 'And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl.' His ear, and not the ear of one who sells himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the piercing פסוק, which talks about one sold by בית דין, says 'his ear'. That word limits piercing to him only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ״אָזְנוֹ״ ('his ear') is read as a מיעוט. It means only this slave, the one sold by בית דין, gets pierced. A מוכר עצמו is left out.

keyTerms.meaning: The תורה limited it (left a case out)
One sold by the court (for stealing)
An awl, a tool for piercing

phrases.english: Because the Merciful One limited it
regarding one sold by the court:
'And his master shall pierce his ear with an awl' —
his ear, of this one,
and not the ear of one who sells himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּמַיעֵט רַחֲמָנָא גַּבֵּי מְכָרוּהוּ בֵּית דִּין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 27 by giving the פסוק.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word ״אָזְנוֹ״ in שמות 21:6 limits piercing to one sold by בית דין.
